item.title: Splitting Requirements at Scale
item.description: Executive summary: The article explains how to split complex requirements into manageable hierarchies without losing traceability, business value, or architectural clarity. It argues for structuring requirements around end-to-end business processes and important problem-domain dimensions, then refining them with consistent abstraction layers so that dependencies stay visible instead of hidden inside individual stories. The main practical message is that good splitting strategy is not just about making requirements smaller; it is about choosing an order and structure that support prioritisation, reuse, and coherent solution design in complex domains.

item.title: How agile can Requirements Engineers really be?
item.description: Executive summary: The article argues that Agile and requirements engineering are not substitutes for one another. In complex telecom projects, Agile ceremonies and user stories can improve collaboration and delivery flow, but they do not remove the need for thorough requirements analysis, dependency management, non-functional specification, and architectural design. The author’s conclusion is that when Agile is treated as a replacement for rigorous RE, hidden dependencies and incomplete analysis can lead to rework, overruns, and quality issues.
